subject: Panacea AI dedicated capacity: tokens/sec model + SLO cushion
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@panacea.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-07T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: dedicated sizing & SLO cushion for Panacea AI pilot

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re kicking off internal planning for a Dedicated deployment (private VPC) to support our beta: Panacea Search API. Before we pull procurement in, we need a best-effort sizing estimate to show execs and engineering. Key things we care about:

- Target SLO: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for single-request chat/query workload (95% of requests are short, ~120 tokens; 5% are longer, ~2k tokens).
- Expected steady-state TPS: ~8 requests/sec across our EU+US traffic, with short spikes at peak up to 24 req/sec (3x).
- Model: we plan to run Optima-13B-quant (4-bit) in the pilot.
- Durability: we need cushion for cold starts and degraded hardware — show a conservative headroom recommendation (safeguard slab).

Can you send tokens/sec estimates per GPU (baseline + quantized), suggested committed slab (GPUs) at the 8 rps and 24 rps scenarios, and recommended SLO guardrails (burst policies, fallback model options)? If you can, attach a quick spreadsheet with the assumptions — CPU/GPU memory, batch sizes, and latency tails.

Also flag any SLA caveats for 3x sustained bursts (>2 minutes). Our procurement asks about minimum commit and how Redwood handles overload.

Appreciate it —
Asha Reddy
Head of Platform
Panacea AI

(attachment: sample_traffic_profile.csv)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Asha Reddy <asha@panacea.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-07T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated sizing & SLO cushion for Panacea AI pilot

Hi Asha —

Thanks — this is the right level of detail. I crunched conservative numbers and attached a one-sheet (panacea_estimate_v1.xlsx) with the assumptions. Summary below — happy to walk through on a quick call.

TL;DR recommendations:
- Baseline GPU SKU: A100x2-equivalent (customer-dedicated slab) running Optima-13B-4bit.
- Steady 8 rps (short-context 120 tokens avg): estimate ~3,400 tokens/sec aggregate required; recommend 2 GPUs reserved (committed slab) to meet p95 <= 350ms with ~35% headroom.
- Peak burst 24 rps (short-context): recommend a burst policy to scale to 4 GPUs (reserved+burst) — committed 2 GPUs + burst to 4 for <1 hour windows.
- Long requests (2k tokens, 5% traffic) drive tail latency — we recommend KV-cache warmup and request shaping: route long requests to a dedicated worker pool (1 extra GPU) or apply a cap that routes >1k token requests to best-effort model variant.

Key estimates / math (see sheet):
- Per-GPU throughput (Optima-13B-4bit, continuous batching, avg batch 4): ~1,800 tokens/sec (p50); p95 effective tokens/sec ~1,300 under observed tail.
- Token-per-request assumptions: short ~120 tokens generated, long ~2,000 tokens.
- Aggregate tokens/sec at 8 rps (short-only): 8 * 120 = 960 tokens/sec generated; we add 2.5x multiplier for overhead/round-trips and concurrent requests => ~2,400 tokens/sec demand. Add 40% safety to handle tails => ~3,400 tokens/sec.

Headroom and SLO fit:
- Committed 2 GPUs: p95 ~300ms for short requests in our sim with warm KV cache; tail events (cold starts or hardware preemption) can push p95 above 350ms.
- If you need contractual p95 <= 350ms with SLA credits, we'd recommend committed 3 GPUs or 2 GPUs + guaranteed burst to 4 with pre-warmed nodes during predictable peak windows.

Operational suggestions:
- Prefix caching for common prompts and model warming during start-of-hour peaks.
- Automatic fallback to Optima-7B-quant for overflow traffic (degrades quality but preserves latency).
- Throttle policy: soft-queue for requests that would exceed configured token budget; return Retry-After when overloaded.

I attached panacea_estimate_v1.xlsx with per-GPU microbenchmarks, quantization impacts, batch-size sensitivity, and a simple cost estimate.

Questions for you:
1) What's the percent of requests that are single-turn vs multi-turn?
2) Are you comfortable with a best-effort fallback model for overflow?
3) Any hard constraints on sustained 3x bursts (>2 minutes)? Procurement will ask.

If useful, I can prepare a 1-page mutual action plan showing commit levels vs cost/SLA tradeoffs.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

(attachment: panacea_estimate_v1.xlsx)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Asha Reddy <asha@panacea.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated sizing & SLO cushion for Panacea AI pilot

Asha / team —

Appreciate the baseline. From a commercial + SLA perspective here’s what we can offer for the pilot (high level):

- Pricing proposal: committed 2 GPU slab at $X, with an option to add burst capacity billed at metered rate. We can offer a 10% pilot discount for the first 3 months tied to a 6-month commitment.
- SLA: Standard dedicated SLA covers 99.9% uptime for the control plane. For p95 latency guarantees (<=350ms) we require either: committed 3 GPUs OR committed 2 GPUs + guaranteed burst to 4 GPUs for peak windows.
- Overload allowance: we can support 3x bursts for short windows (<=120s) without SLA penalty. For sustained bursts >2 minutes, we treat as a capacity event and will engage escalation — we can commit a remediation timeline but not SLA credits unless pre-provisioned capacity is purchased.

Next steps from our side: we’ll prepare a Mutual Action Plan and a refined spreadsheet that ties the pricing line-items to the headroom assumptions (I’ll attach panacea_slo_diff.docx). Ben, can you add any operational caveats or onboarding timelines?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
On a practical note: if Panacea expects the 5% long-request traffic to be unpredictable, allocate an extra GPU (or isolate long requests to a separate pool) — it materially reduces p95 for short queries without raising cost dramatically.

(attachment: panacea_slo_diff.docx)

From: Dominic Lee <dominic.lee@panacea.ai>

Date: 2027-04-10T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated sizing & SLO cushion for Panacea AI pilot

Thanks everyone —

Appreciate the clear analysis. Quoting Jonas for clarity:

> TL;DR recommendations:
> - Baseline GPU SKU: A100x2-equivalent running Optima-13B-4bit.
> - Steady 8 rps: recommend 2 GPUs committed with ~35% headroom.
> - Peak 24 rps: burst to 4 GPUs (committed 2 + burst).
> - Long requests (2k tokens) should be isolated or routed to a variant model.

We’re broadly aligned internally. A few clarifying asks before we move to procurement:
1) Can you add a second tab in the spreadsheet that shows 3 scenarios (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive) with committed GPUs and monthly cost?
2) For the fallback Optima-7B option, what is expected quality delta (high-level) — is it acceptable for search-quality fallback for 10% of requests?
3) Can we schedule a 30-minute negotiation call next week? Thursdays 10–12 or Friday 9–11 PT work for us.

If you confirm the scenario sheet and the pricing rows, we’ll route this to procurement.

Thanks —
Dominic Lee
VP Engineering
Panacea AI
